cli.help.title: zinc: apps, games and boards in typed TypeScript
cli.help.more: More: zinc help --all lists every command; zinc help <command> describes one.
cli.help.project: In a project folder, zinc run, zinc build and zinc check need no argument.
cli.help.options: With any command: -v shows the steps and their durations (-vv more), -q hides them, --lang en|fr|es|it|de chooses the language, --background opens windows without taking the focus, --log-format json prints one JSON object per line.
cli.help.log: ZINC_LOG=<module>=<level>,... chooses what -v shows (modules build, plugin, run, ui; levels info, debug, trace), for example ZINC_LOG=ui=debug for the layout passes.
cli.help.engine: For work on the engine itself: lex, parse, ir, zbc, bake, profile, mem, device-sim, --version, --emit=cpp|zbc.

cli.tour.title: Zinc tour: eight short steps in a real project. q stops at any time, and zinc tour goes on from there.
cli.tour.s4: Make a mistake and read it
cli.tour.new.do: zinc new makes a project from a template. The tour takes the game template: a square that the arrow keys move.
cli.tour.new.missing: no project was made (no zinc.json and src/main.ts)
cli.tour.new.done: Your project is {dir}: zinc.json describes it, src/main.ts is the program.
cli.tour.run.do: zinc run compiles the program and runs it: a window opens and the arrow keys move the square. Close the window to come back here.
cli.tour.run.auto: zinc run compiles the program and runs it (here without a window, for a few frames).
cli.tour.run.failed: zinc run ended with the code {code}
cli.tour.run.done: It runs: zinc run ended without an error.
cli.tour.edit.do: Open src/main.ts in your editor. On the line with `arrows to move`, write your name in place of those words, then save.
cli.tour.edit.done: Saved, and zinc check finds no error. Your line: {line}
cli.tour.waiting: The tour waits for your save. Enter checks now, s skips this step, q stops.
cli.tour.mistake.do: Now a mistake, on purpose: on the first line of src/main.ts, change `isDown` to `isDwon`, then save.
cli.tour.mistake.none: zinc check finds no error yet
cli.tour.mistake.seen: zinc check found it. It gives the file, the line, the column and an error code:
cli.tour.mistake.explain: Every error code has its explanation: {command} prints it.
cli.tour.mistake.undo: Now fix it: put `isDown` back, then save.
cli.tour.mistake.done: Fixed: zinc check finds no error again.
cli.tour.dev.do: zinc dev runs the program and watches its files. The tour starts it and a window opens. Change the text in src/main.ts again and save: the window shows it at once, and the square stays where it was. This is Fast Refresh.
cli.tour.dev.auto: zinc dev runs the program and watches its files: the tour starts it and saves a change.
cli.tour.dev.wait: zinc dev has not shown a save yet
cli.tour.dev.done: zinc dev changed the program while it ran: {line}
cli.tour.dev.stop: Press Enter when you have seen it: the tour stops zinc dev and closes the window.
cli.tour.kind.do: Zinc makes games, apps with windows, command-line tools, servers, 3D scenes and programs for boards. Which one fits your idea: {url}
cli.tour.kind.ask: Press Enter: zinc new asks what to make, beside the tour's project (s skips this step, q stops).
cli.tour.kind.none: no new project beside the tour's project
cli.tour.kind.done: {dir} is ready, and zinc check finds no error. Go into its folder and start zinc dev.
cli.tour.docs.learn: Twelve short lessons, from a shape in a window to a small game: {url}
cli.tour.docs.help: In the terminal: zinc help lists the commands, zinc help dev describes one, zinc explain lists the error codes.
cli.tour.docs.ask: Press Enter to open the lessons in your browser (s goes on without them, q stops).
cli.tour.docs.failed: the browser did not open: copy the link above
cli.tour.atelier.do: Zinc Atelier is the editor made for Zinc: write, run and see your program in one window. It is installed here: {app}
cli.tour.atelier.ask: Press Enter to open the tour's project in it (s skips this step, q stops).
cli.tour.atelier.missing: Zinc Atelier is the editor made for Zinc: write, run and see your program in one window. It is not installed here; the installer adds it with --atelier: {command}
cli.tour.next: Press Enter for step {n} (q stops here, and zinc tour goes on from there).
cli.tour.enter: Press Enter to go on (s skips this step, q stops).
cli.tour.stopped: Stopped at step {n}. zinc tour goes on from there; zinc tour --list shows the steps.
cli.tour.end: That was the tour. Next, the lessons: {url}
cli.tour.all_done: You have done every step. zinc tour 1 walks them again; zinc tour --reset starts over with a new project.
cli.tour.first: Step 1 comes first: it makes the project the other steps use.
cli.tour.list.title: zinc tour: {done} of {total} steps done
cli.tour.list.how: zinc tour goes on, zinc tour 5 goes to step 5, zinc tour --reset starts over.
cli.tour.noterm: zinc tour asks you things and waits for you: start it in a terminal. zinc tour --auto does every step by itself.
cli.tour.reset: The tour starts over. Its project stays in {dir}.
cli.tour.no_step: zinc tour: the steps are 1 to {total}
